requirements.section: line 45 (locator only; exact passage is authoritative)
requirements.sentence: **Python 2.** No lexical rule can tell Python 2 from Python 3 without a parser: `print "x"` and `exec code` lex as a name followed by a string or name. A Python 2 file is therefore lexed by the Python 3.14 rules. Most lex and are fingerprinted with Python 3 token classes (`print` is `ident`). Some fail with an ordinary lexical error: backticks (`illegal-character`), `ur''` (`malformed-literal`), `0777` and `1L` (`malformed-literal`), and tab/space mixtures (`inconsistent-indentation`). This is the "unavoidable" case: the selecting tool SHOULD exclude a repository whose metadata declares Python 2 (for example `python_requires` below 3), and MUST NOT silently drop files that fail.

clauses.reason: Silently dropping a file is a selection/pipeline behavior outside the extraction record; requires repository-level accounting.

requirements.sentence: - **Explicit.** Outside literals and comments, `\` MUST be immediately followed by a line terminator, and that line terminator MUST NOT be the last thing in the input. Then `\` and the terminator are skipped and the next physical line continues the logical line; its leading white space is ordinary white space. Anything else is `illegal-character` at the `\`: a stray backslash (`py-err-backslash-stray`), and a continuation that ends the input (`py-err-backslash-eof`; CPython: "unexpected EOF"). `\` CR LF is one continuation (`py-crlf-continuation`). A backslash inside a comment is part of the comment and does not continue it.

requirements.section: line 132 (locator only; exact passage is authoritative)
requirements.sentence: **Layout-only k-grams and empty spans.** Because these tokens are zero-width, a k-gram made only of layout tokens can have an **empty span**. At the default k = 5 this happens whenever a file ends four or more blocks deep: the last k-gram is NEWLINE followed by four DEDENTs, all at the input length, so its span is `[n, n)`, and it can be selected as a fingerprint (`py-empty-span-fingerprint`: span `[35, 35)`; the checker requires an empty-span fingerprint there). Layout-only k-grams inside a file have non-empty spans that cover only white space and comments. Such k-grams are identical across unrelated files and will be common hashes. **What the catalogue contract must say:** an empty span is a valid fingerprint span for `py-tokens` at every k, not only at k = 1, so a catalogue MUST store and a report MUST carry `[n, n)` unchanged, and a consumer MUST NOT treat it as an error or drop it. How M2 localization and suppression should treat layout-only k-grams belongs to the matching contract.

requirements.sentence: **Prefix.** When a name (§3.2) is immediately followed by `'` or `"`, and its text, compared case-insensitively, consists only of the letters `b`, `r`, `u`, `f`, `t` with no letter repeated, it is a prefix. The letter set MUST be one of {b}, {r}, {u}, {f}, {t}, {b, r}, {f, r}, {t, r}, in any order and case; any other set (`ur`, `ub`, `bf`, `bt`, `ft`, three letters) is `malformed-literal` at the prefix start. A name with any other letter, or a repeated letter, is an ordinary name followed by a separate string: `uu'x'`, `rr"y"`, `print'z'`, `bx'w'` (`py-prefix-ident`). requirements.sentence: Brackets, f/t-strings, replacement fields and nested format-spec fields nest without a depth limit (D-9), so the only bound is `maxInputBytes`: about 350,000 levels within 1 MiB, 2.8 million within the 8 MiB contract bound. **An implementation MUST track nesting with an explicit stack, in memory linear in the input size (contract §10a).
